rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative is a rebuke, and the proposed new creation means resurrection.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام للإنكار، والخلق الجديد هو البعث.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift with بل clarifies that their denial is not fundamentally an argument from inability: they disbelieve in return to God and meeting Him.
rows.anchor: بل هم كافرون بالرجوع إلينا ولقائنا ولذا جيء في الجواب عن قولهم بما يدل على الرجوع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawaffī means taking something completely, as when a debt is collected in full.
rows.anchor: توفي الشيء أخذه تاما كاملا كتوفي الحق وتوفي الدين من المديون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported gloss takes the assigned angel as charged with causing death and taking souls, but the verse's unrestricted wording appears broader.
rows.anchor: قيل أي وكل بإماتتكم وقبض أرواحكم والآية مطلقة ظاهرة في أعم من ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an attributes taking souls to God, the angel of death, and the angelic messengers because they occupy different levels in the causal hierarchy.
rows.anchor: وقد نسب التوفي في الآية إلى ملك الموت، وفي قوله والله يتوفى الأنفس حين موتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers are the angel of death's assistants; he executes God's command, while God is the ultimate cause behind all causes.
rows.anchor: فالسبب القريب الملائكة الرسل أعوان ملك الموت وفوقهم ملك الموت الآمر بذلك المجري لأمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The layered attribution resembles writing: the pen, hand, and person can each be called a writer.
rows.anchor: فذلك بوجه كمثل كتابة الإنسان بالقلم فالقلم كاتب واليد كاتبة والإنسان كاتب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return to God is the meeting mentioned in the prior verse, namely resurrection after death; ثم marks its temporal delay after death.
rows.anchor: هو الرجوع الذي عبر عنه في الآية السابقة باللقاء وموطنه البعث المترتب على التوفي والمتراخي عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Simply saying the angel takes souls would leave resurrection as an unsupported claim, so the reply addresses the objection that the dead disappear or bodily dissolution erases identity.
rows.anchor: والآية - على أي تقدير - جواب عن الاحتجاج بضلال الموتى في الأرض على نفي البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death is not human annihilation: the angel takes the complete self from the body, while only bodies decay; the self remains preserved until God restores it to its body for judgment and recompense.
rows.anchor: بل ملك الموت الموكل بكم يأخذكم تامين كاملين من أجسادكم أي ينزع أرواحكم من أبدانكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human essence is the self referred to by “I,” distinct from and primary over the body; it does not perish at death, so bodily dissolution does not eliminate the person.
rows.anchor: وهي لا تتلاشى بالموت ولا تنعدم بل محفوظة في قدرة الله حتى يؤذن في رجوعها

rows.speaker: ملك الموت
rows.claim: In a report about the Prophet visiting an Anṣārī, the angel says he is gentle with every believer, encounters every household five times daily, and cannot take even a mosquito's soul without God's command.
rows.anchor: فإذا ملك الموت عند رأسه فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يا ملك الموت ارفق بصاحبي

rows.speaker: تفسير القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummī glosses God's statement that He could have given every soul its guidance as meaning that He could have made them all infallible.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { ولو شئنا لآتينا كل نفس هداها } قال لو شئنا أن نجعلهم كلهم معصومين لقدرنا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Infallibility does not conflict with free choice, so the cited report does not conflict with the author's prior interpretation of the verse.
rows.anchor: أقول العصمة لا تنافي الاختيار فلا تنافي بين مضمون الرواية وما قدمناه في تفسير الآية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic verses strongly indicate that present humanity descends through reproduction from one particular man and woman, named Adam, who were created from earth without parents; descent from Adam is Qur'anically certain, though the exact sense of Adam is unsettled.
rows.anchor: أن البشر الموجودين اليوم - ونحن منهم - ينتهون بالتناسل إلى زوج أي رجل وامرأة بعينهما وقد سمي الرجل في القرآن بآدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses are highly evident but not explicit beyond all possible interpretation, and the specific meaning of Adam is not a religious necessity even if humanity's descent from Adam may be Qur'anically necessary.
rows.anchor: فهذا هو الذي يفيده الآيات ظهورا معتدا به وإن لم تكن نصة صريحة لا تقبل التأويل ولا المسألة من ضروريات الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unresolved alternatives are a collective human type, a finite group of first ancestors, or one individual Adam; the individual model itself allows different proposed routes of emergence from earlier forms of life.
rows.anchor: هل أريد به آدم النوعي أعني الطبيعة الإنسانية الفاشية في الأشخاص أو عدة معدودة من الأفراد هم أصول النسب والأباء والأمهات الأولية أو فرد إنساني واحد بالشخص؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed model makes a fully rational human the first of the accountable human kind, emerging by reproduction from a less rational human kind that had itself developed through earlier animal forms.
rows.anchor: فكان مبدأ لظهور النوع الإنساني المجهز بالتعقل القابل للتكليف وانفصاله من النوع غير المجهز بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent Qur'anic reading is that present humanity descends from Adam and his wife, both formed from earth without a father or mother.
rows.anchor: فظاهر الآيات القرآنية هو الصورة الأخيرة وهي انتهاء النسل الحاضر إلى آدم وزوجه المتكونين من الأرض من غير أب وأم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses do not specify how Adam was created: it may have involved extraordinary causes or an immediate divine formation, or a gradual process through successive bodily potentials until the spirit was breathed in, comparable in conditions to embryonic formation.
rows.anchor: غير أن الآيات لم تبين كيفية خلق آدم من الأرض وأنه هل عملت في خلقه علل وعوامل خارقة للعادة؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'an 3:59 compares Jesus with Adam because Adam was created from the earth without a parent; otherwise the comparison would have no special force against the claim that Jesus' father was God.
rows.anchor: ومن أوضح الدليل عليه قوله تعالى إن مثل عيسى عند الله كمثل آدم خلقه من تراب ثم قال له كن فيكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation that Adam merely traces back to earth like everyone else destroys the point of comparing him with Jesus, since it gives Adam no distinctive status.
rows.anchor: ومن المعلوم أن لا خصوصية لآدم على هذا المعنى حتى يؤخذ ويقاس إليه عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other descriptions of Adam's creation from clay support creation without parents, including the statement that God will create a human from clay and that He began human creation from clay.
rows.anchor: خلق آدم من تراب أو طين أو نحو ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The collective-Adam reading treats the Garden story as an imaginative portrayal of human nature's closeness to God and its later fall through desire and obedience to Satan, but the author says this is defeated by the preceding argument and the verses' plain wording.
rows.anchor: وأما قول من قال إن المراد بآدم هو آدم النوعي دون الشخصي بمعنى الطبيعة الإنسانية الخارجية الفاشية في الأفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam as a collective human nature is contradicted by the verse that God made a spouse from one soul and spread many men and women from the pair, as well as the accounts of Adam and his wife in the Garden.
rows.anchor: فلو كان المراد بالنفس الواحدة آدم النوعي لم يبق لفرض الزوج لها محل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The collective-Adam view depends on an ancient earth and eternally established species with indefinitely many individuals, assumptions the author says scientific principles decisively disprove.
rows.anchor: على أن أصل القول بآدم النوعي مبني على قدم الأرض والأنواع المتأصلة ومنها الإنسان وأن أفراده غير متناهية من الجانبين والأصول العلمية تبطل ذلك بتاتا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposal that current humanity descends from several limited couples, divided by skin color or by old and newly discovered lands, cannot fit the verses' descent from Adam and his wife; its assumptions about separate human species and permanently divided continents are disproven.
rows.anchor: وأما القول بكون النسل منتهيا إلى أفراد معدودين كأربعة أزواج مختلفين ببياض اللون وسواده وحمرته وصفرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects descent through an earlier animal kind such as an ape because the relevant verses describe the first human as created from clay without parents; he also says the scientific proof for this model is insufficient.
rows.anchor: ففيه أن الآيات السابقة الدالة على خلق الإنسان الأول من تراب من غير أب وأم تدفعه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposal that two fully rational humans evolved from a non-rational human kind and survived after the original kind went extinct is contradicted by the Adam-from-earth comparison with Jesus.
rows.anchor: فيدفعه قوله تعالى { إن مثل عيسى عند الله كمثل آدم خلقه من تراب ثم قال له كن فيكون } على التقريب المتقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Proponents cite comparative anatomy, animal embryos, and fossils as signs of gradual changes in the features and organs of species, with simpler animals appearing earlier than more complex ones.
rows.anchor: فإنها شواهد مأخوذة من التشريح التطبيقي وأجنة الحيوان والآثار الحفرية الدالة على التغير التدريجي في صفات الأنواع وأعضائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those observations show matter gradually becoming prepared to receive different animal forms, not that a complete animal kind genealogically descended from another; no such birth of one kind from another has been observed.
rows.anchor: فهي قد استعدت لظهور الحياة الكاملة فيها بعد الناقصة والشريفة بعد الخسيسة وأما كون الكامل من الحيوان منشعبا من الناقص بالتولد والاتصال النسبي فلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The observed gradual fossil changes are changes within one kind, moving from one trait to another without leaving that kind; the proposed claim requires a change between kinds.
rows.anchor: فإنما هو تغير في نوع واحد بالانتقال من صفة لها إلى صفة أخرى لا يخرج بذلك عن نوعيته والمدعى خلاف ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life has levels of greater and lesser perfection and nobility, with human life at the highest level, followed by successively lesser forms.
rows.anchor: فالذي يتسلم أن نشأة الحياة ذات مراتب مختلفة بالكمال والنقص والشرف والخسة وأعلى مراتبها الحياة الإنسانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evidence does not establish that each kind changed into a neighboring, more perfect kind; evolution remains a conjectural, non-certain hypothesis in natural science that could change with further research.
rows.anchor: فالقول بتبدل الأنواع بالتطور فرضية حدسية تبتني عليها العلوم الطبيعية اليوم ومن الممكن أن يتغير يوما إلى خلافها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An argument for evolution reads Adam's selection with Noah and the families of Abraham and ʿImrān as choosing him from a group of earlier, non-rational humans.
rows.anchor: وربما استدل على هذا القول بقوله تعالى إن الله اصطفى آدم ونوحا وآل إبراهيم وآل عمران على العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author replies that “the worlds” is universal and can include all people contemporary with and subsequent to each chosen figure, as in the Prophet being mercy to all worlds; thus Adam need not have been selected from a pre-rational species.
rows.anchor: وهو يفيد العموم ويصدق على عامة البشر إلى يوم القيامة فهم مصطفون على جميع المعاصرين لهم والجائين بعدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if selection were limited to contemporaries, Adam could have been chosen from among his contemporaneous descendants; the verse does not say his selection occurred before he had children.
rows.anchor: ولا دلالة في الآية على كون اصطفائه أول خلقته قبل ولادة أولاده.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Adam was selected because he had reason while earlier humans lacked it, that trait would also belong to his descendants, leaving no basis for singling Adam out in the verse.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك بما أنه مجهز بالعقل وكان ذلك مشتركا بينه وبين بني آدم جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One argument reads the ثم in Qur'an 7:11 as temporal and infers that humanity existed before Adam and the angels' command to bow.
rows.anchor: بناء على أن { ثم } تدل على التراخي الزماني فقد كان للنوع الإنساني وجود قبل خلق آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says ثم in 7:11 orders the discourse rather than events in time, a frequent Qur'anic usage; he also points to another interpretation discussed earlier in the book.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن { ثم } في الآية للترتيب الكلامي وهو كثير الورود في كلامه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second argument reads the sequence from clay to offspring from a fluid and then full formation and spirit as allowing a substantial interval for intermediate species, especially because سلالة is indefinite.
rows.anchor: وتقريبه أن الآية الأولى المتعرضة لأول خلق الإنسان تذكر خلقته الأولية من تراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads the sequence as Adam beginning from clay, his offspring arising from a fluid, and creation then being completed by shaping and the spirit, in Adam or his offspring; this requires no intermediate species.
rows.anchor: والآيات في مقام بيان ظهور النوع الإنساني بالخلق وأن بدأ خلقه وهو خلق آدم كان من طين ثم بدل سلالة من ماء في ظهور أولاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An indefinite noun such as سلالة does not imply generality in an affirmative statement; it does so only in a negative context.
rows.anchor: وكون { سلالة } نكرة لا يستلزم العموم فإن إفادة النكرة للعموم إنما هو فيما إذا وقعت في سياق النفي دون الإثبات.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage exhorts believers to remember and glorify God, promises them good, and addresses the Prophet with noble attributes; the two groups may have been revealed at different times.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون القبيلان مختلفين في النزول زمانا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr is the opposite of forgetfulness: directing one's perception toward the thing remembered; speaking its names and attributes is only one instance of remembrance.
rows.anchor: الذكر ما يقابل النسيان وهو توجيه الإدراك نحو المذكور وأما التلفظ بما يدل عليه من أسمائه وصفاته فهو بعض مصاديق الذكر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ means declaring God transcendent; like remembrance it need not be verbal, though saying phrases such as سبحان الله is one form of it.
rows.anchor: التسبيح هو التنزيه وهو مثل الذكر لا يتوقف على اللفظ وإن كان التلفظ بمثل سبحان الله بعض مصاديق التسبيح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Morning means the day's beginning and evening its later part after ʿAṣr; these periods suit glorifying God beyond changing conditions and passing defects, and together may signify continual praise, as in 41:38.
rows.anchor: وتقييد التسبيح بالبكرة والأصيل لما فيهما من تحول الأحوال فيناسب تسبيحه وتنزيهه من التغير والتحول وكل نقص طار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shared sense of ṣalāh is turning or inclination, with its meaning varying by agent: mercy from God, seeking forgiveness from angels, and supplication from people; God's Qur'anic ṣalāh is special mercy to believers that yields lasting felicity.
rows.anchor: المعنى الجامع للصلاة على ما يستفاد من موارد استعمالها هو الانعطاف فيختلف باختلاف ما نسب إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's special mercy turns believers from darkness into light and brings the lasting success of the afterlife; this explains the stated purpose of His ṣalāh upon them.
rows.anchor: وهي التي تترتب عليها سعادة العقبى والفلاح المؤبد ولذلك علل تصليته عليهم بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an pairs people's forgetting God with God's leaving them and their remembering Him with His remembering them; His ṣalāh is remembrance through mercy, light, and removal from darkness.
rows.anchor: تصليته عليهم ذكر منه لهم بالرحمة فإن ذكروه كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 43 explains the command in verse 41: abundant remembrance brings abundant divine mercy and light; darkness means forgetfulness and heedlessness, while light means remembrance.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن قوله { هو الذي يصلي عليكم } الخ، في مقام التعليل لقوله { يا أيها الذين آمنوا اذكروا الله ذكرا كثيرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit phrase “with the believers,” instead of a pronoun meaning “with you,” identifies faith as the reason for God's mercy.
rows.anchor: وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر، أعني قوله { بالمؤمنين } ولم يقل وكان بكم رحيما، ليدل به على سبب الرحمة وهو وصف الإيمان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their greeting is grammatically an object-annexed verbal noun: they are greeted by God and His angels with peace when they meet their Lord, and are safe from harm and punishment.
rows.anchor: ظاهر السياق أن { تحيتهم } مصدر مضاف إلى المفعول أي إنهم يحيون - بالبناء للمفعول - يوم يلقون ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised generous reward is a great recompense prepared for them by God.
rows.anchor: أي وهيأ الله لهم ثوابا جزيلا.

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet calls abundant remembrance the best of deeds, highest in rank, purest with God, and better than wealth or fighting and dying in battle.
rows.anchor: ألا أخبركم بخير أعمالكم أرفعها في درجاتكم وأزكاها عند مليككم وخير لكم من الدينار والدرهم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Asked who is best among the mosque's people, the Prophet answers: those who remember God most.
rows.anchor: جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فقال من خير أهل المسجد؟ فقال أكثرهم لله ذكرا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The person granted a remembering tongue has been granted the good of this world and the next.
rows.anchor: من أعطي لسانا ذاكرا فلقد أعطي خير الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: An unattributed gloss of “do not give in order to receive more” says not to regard one's good work for God as abundant.
rows.anchor: لا تستكثر ما عملت من خير لله

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report raised by Abū al-Muʿazzā says private remembrance counts as abundant remembrance, while hypocrites remember publicly but not privately, as in 4:142.
rows.anchor: وفيه بإسناده عن أبي المعزا رفعه قال قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام من ذكر الله في السر فقد ذكر الله كثيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls the inference from the hypocrites' public-only remembrance a subtle one.
rows.anchor: أقول وهو استفادة لطيفة.

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Through Zayd al-Shahhām, al-Ṣādiq names three especially severe tests for a believer: giving from one's wealth, fairness to oneself, and abundant remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: عن زيد الشحام قال قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام ما ابتلي المؤمن بشيء أشد عليه من ثلاث خصال يحرمها

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abundant remembrance includes remembering God when facing what He permits and what He forbids, so that one obeys His limits.
rows.anchor: ولكن ذكر الله عند ما أحل له وذكر الله عندما حرم عليه.

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Remembering God is not limited to repeating phrases such as glorification, praise, the testimony of divine unity, and magnification, though those phrases are included.
rows.anchor: أما إني لا أقول سبحان الله والحمد لله ولا إله إلا الله والله أكبر وإن كان منه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: In a report from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī recorded by Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī, and al-Bayhaqī, the Prophet says those who remember God much outrank even a warrior who fights until his sword breaks and is bloodied.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم سئل أي العباد أفضل درجة عند الله يوم القيامة؟

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: In a report transmitted through al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, the Prophet explains that he is a caller because he invites people to his Lord's religion.
rows.anchor: فقال صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أما الداعي فإني أدعو الناس إلى دين ربي عز وجل

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet explains that he is a warner because he warns those who disobey him of the Fire.
rows.anchor: وأما النذير فإني أنذر بالنار من عصاني

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet explains that he is a bearer of good news because he promises Paradise to those who obey him.
rows.anchor: وأما البشير فإني أبشر بالجنة من أطاعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to challenge the claimed deities by asking them for help: دعاء here means asking them for a need, while زعمتم omits its two objects because context supplies “you claimed them gods.”
rows.anchor: ودعاؤهم هو مسألتهم شيئا من الحوائج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot answer because they own not even an atom; if they owned anything needed by people, they could give it, thereby qualifying as lords or gods and deserving worship in gratitude.
rows.anchor: ولا تتم الربوبية والألوهية إلا بأن يملك الرب والإله شيئا مما يحتاج إليه الإنسان فيملكه له وينعم عليه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first denial negates unrestricted ownership of the heavens and earth; the next negates limited, partial ownership, whether shared jointly or divided into portions.
rows.anchor: كان الملك المنفي في الجملة السابقة { لا يملكون } الخ، الملك المطلق المنبسط على الجميع والمنفي في هذه الجملة الملك المحدود المتبعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists did not claim undivided co-ownership with God; they assigned each deity a kind or part of creation while treating God as Lord of lords and God of gods.
rows.anchor: بل كانوا يقولون بملك كل من آلهتهم لنوع من الخلقة أو بعض منها، وأما الله سبحانه فهو رب الأرباب وإله الآلهة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If their gods owned particular parts of creation, they should answer prayers concerning those parts; their failure to do so shows they are no lords or gods.
rows.anchor: وعدم استجابتهم كاشف عن عدم ربوبيتهم وألوهيتهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial that God has a supporter among them means none assists Him, wholly or partly, where He might be unable to govern; such a supporter would own something and answer prayers concerning it.
rows.anchor: أي ليس لله سبحانه منهم كلا أو بعضا من معين يعينه فيما يفرض فيه عجزه عن القيام بأمر تدبيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument through failure to answer supplication applies across all three proposed relations: total ownership, shared or partial ownership, and being God's helper in governance.
rows.anchor: أن احتجاج الآية على نفي الملك بانتفاء استجابتهم دعاء الداعي يجري في جميع الصور الثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists also claimed that their deities could intercede; the author introduces the next verse's restriction of intercession and cites the Qur'an's account of this belief.
rows.anchor: المشركون كانوا يقولون بشفاعة آلهتهم كما حكاه الله سبحانه عنهم بقوله

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās, also transmitted by Ibn al-Mundhir from Abū Hurayra, lists five privileges: universal mission, victory through fear, lawful spoils, the earth as a mosque and purification, and intercession reserved for the Prophet's community through the Resurrection for those who do not associate partners with God.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أعطيت خمسا لم يعطهن نبي قبلى بعثت إلى الناس كافة الأحمر والأسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report's claim that no earlier prophet was sent to all humanity conflicts with widely transmitted reports that Noah had a universal mission, and reports naming Abraham or all messengers of firm resolve as universal messengers.
rows.anchor: والرواية معارضة لما ورد مستفيضا أن نوحا كان مبعوثا إلى الناس كافة وذكر في بعضها إبراهيم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report also conflicts with the broad prophetic intercession indicated by multiple narrations and by the Qur'an's exception for those who bear witness to the truth knowingly; the Qur'an identifies Jesus as a witness over them.
rows.anchor: وتخالف أيضا عموم الشفاعة للأنبياء المستفاد من عدة من الروايات وقد قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many reports in both Sunni and Shiʿi sources establish the Prophet's universal mission; the apparent grammar of كافة in 34:28 makes it a circumstantial accusative from للناس, fronted, which Basran grammarians disallow and Kufan grammarians permit.
rows.anchor: وظاهر كثير منها أخذ { كافة } في قوله تعالى { وما أرسلناك إلا كافة للناس } حالا من { للناس } قدم عليه ويمنعه البصريون من النحاة ويجوزه الكوفيون.
